parsed.ranking_rationale: Candidate-f is the only architecture that achieves both mechanical correctness and semantic excellence. It correctly assigns the protocol state machine to the session module, uses frozen headers as task-ready contract interfaces, and maintains a valid DAG. Candidate-e has excellent responsibility cohesion but fails contract boundaries by using .c source files as interface files. Candidates-c and candidate-b suffer from severe responsibility cohesion issues, turning the application entry point into a protocol god-object while reducing the session module to a dumb data store; candidate-c further penalizes itself with .c interface files. Candidates-d and candidate-a share the god-object flaw and additionally contain critical DAG errors where the application work package declares no dependencies despite consuming all other modules.

strengths: Excellent separation of concerns: session module owns the protocol state machine, codec owns wire format, and net owns I/O.
Correctly leverages frozen headers as task-ready contract interfaces, bridging s5 generation and s6 implementation seamlessly.
Valid, acyclic DAG with correct work package dependencies.
Comprehensive and accurate requirement ownership mapping.

blocking_findings: Uses .c source files as interface_files in contracts, violating C header-based boundary conventions and the delivery constraints' internal interface slots.
strengths: Strong responsibility cohesion with the session module correctly owning the broker state machine and protocol logic.
Valid DAG with appropriate work package dependencies.

blocking_findings: Application module acts as a god-object for protocol logic, leaving the session module as a mere subscription data store.
Uses .c source files for implementation contracts, which is an anti-pattern for C interface boundaries.
strengths: Valid DAG and explicit contract gating.
Clear distinction between s5 frozen headers and s6 owned sources.

blocking_findings: Application module is a god-object that implements almost all protocol orchestration, severely violating responsibility cohesion and defeating the purpose of a dedicated session module.
strengths: Valid DAG with correct work package dependencies.
Standard and correct usage of s5 contracts and header interfaces.

blocking_findings: Critical DAG error: wp-app has an empty depends_on array despite consuming all other modules and contracts.
Application module is a god-object handling protocol logic that belongs in the session module.
strengths: Clear module definitions and correct identification of s5 frozen artifacts.

blocking_findings: Critical DAG error: wp-app has no dependencies despite consuming all other modules.
Network module has an empty requirement_responsibilities array, missing transport and connection lifecycle ownership.
Application module acts as a god-object for protocol orchestration.
strengths: Basic module structure correctly identifies the four primary domains (codec, session, net, app).
